checks.detail: ANSWER.md cites MSG-102, not returned by any tool and not in the inputs

items.reasoning: In ledger A1 the agent ran update_ticket and moved the existing ticket NBL-042 from 'completed' to mp_time. The note reads 'Reopened: tenant reports on 2024-03-04 (event 032) fix did not hold'. This treats the report as the same fault on the same job.
items.evidence: A1 update_ticket stage mp_time, note 'Reopened... fix did not hold'

items.reasoning: In A2 (MSG-101, verified) the agent emailed Lantern Services. The message says the repair worked for a couple of washes but the water has not heated for about 5 days, and asks the provider to arrange a return visit. It also asks 'whether this is covered as a repeat of your earlier repair' and tells them not to do any new chargeable work without a quote and approval. It does not name the wiring repair or the £75 + VAT figure. It also asks about warranty cover rather than stating the revisit is free. Even so, the message achieves the intended outcome: the same provider is sent back, the visit is framed as rework of their earlier repair, and the reported failure after about five days is included.
items.evidence: A2: 'Please let us know whether this is covered as a repeat of your earlier repair, and do not proceed to any new chargeable work without a quote and our approval.'

items.reasoning: In A4 (MSG-103, verified) the landlord email says the fault has come back and that the provider has been asked to return and confirm whether the revisit is covered under the earlier repair. It adds: 'If any new chargeable work is needed, we will send you a quote for approval first.' That covers recurrence, no further cost expected, and approval for any charge.
In A3 (MSG-105, verified after one retry) the tenant is told: 'sorry the fix didn't hold... asked Lantern Services to come back... no date is confirmed yet'. No date was invented.
The agent did not escalate a repair-versus-replace decision. It stated that no escalation was needed.
The tenant message did not ask which cycles fail or for any error codes.
The agent flagged a mismatch in the invoice amount (£75.11 vs £75 + VAT) and asked for the PDF. It did not put the invoice on hold or mark it as disputed pending the return visit.
items.evidence: Remaining work: 'Earlier invoice... should be reconciled'

items.reasoning: The ticket note records the recurrence date (2024-03-04) and that the fix did not hold. It does not record what the previous repair was (wiring to the heating element) or when it was done.

The provider was asked to 'reply with the date you confirm'. They were not asked to report what they find on the return visit; they were only asked about warranty cover. So only half of this item is met.
No fresh chargeable job was raised. The failed fix is mentioned in every message.
The ticket was reopened, and the tenant was not told the job is complete.
No payment was approved. The agent explicitly said any new chargeable work needs a quote and approval first.
The landlord email clearly states that the first repair failed.
The report was acted on: the ticket was reopened, three messages were sent and a follow-up was scheduled.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled the recurrence well. It reopened the job, sent the same provider back with a warranty framing, kept the landlord's approval in place for any new charge, and gave the tenant an honest update. It fell short on detail: the prior wiring repair is not recorded in the case notes, the provider is not asked to report findings, and the invoice is not put on hold pending the revisit.
